tldr: A formal Lean-community certification of a Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof and new open-source runtime integrations mark major developments in AI-assisted mathematics and practical multimodal tooling.

Catch-up research on small-agent planning, single-pass distilled decision models, robotic risk control and video generation is promising but remains benchmark- and author-dependent; infrastructure plans and real-world self-driving recalls require careful date and evidence labels.

news.title: Lean and Mathlib teams certify a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis
news.summary: A November 21 joint Lean/Mathlib statement reports independent checks of Levent Alpöge's enormous Lean proof released November 20, including statement matching and multiple proof kernels. Alpöge credits collaboration with Claude.
news.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a striking use of AI-assisted mathematics plus machine-verifiable proofs, with independent checks separating a claimed breakthrough from model-generated plausibility.
news.caveat: Formal checking validates a theorem relative to mathematical foundations and the exact statement; independent conceptual exposition and broader mathematical scrutiny can continue. The Lean organizations' certification does not by itself establish how much of the discovery was caused by AI.

news.title: Transformers v5.24 adds native support for looped, audio and multimodal architectures
news.summary: Hugging Face's November 21 v5.24.0 release documents support for Inkling 2 Mini, Apertus 1.5, WavTokenizer, Dory, HY4-VL, Omnilingual ASR and Lara Mini.
news.why_it_matters: New architecture integrations can reduce custom implementation work and give researchers more standard loading paths for varied speech, vision and small-model systems.
news.caveat: This is a library compatibility release, not proof that each model first launched on November 21; weights, gated access, license and device memory vary by model.

news.title: llama.cpp adds Kyutai Hibiki real-time duplex support
news.summary: The ggml-org b12619 release adds mtmd support for Kyutai Hibiki real-time duplex, including a long-session-quality fix and a Metal fusion regression baseline.
news.why_it_matters: Extends local inference plumbing for simultaneous listening and speaking workloads, a distinct path from fixed-turn ASR-LLM-TTS chains.
news.caveat: The release note documents implementation support, not measured end-to-end latency or stability across all devices; specific model checkpoints and compute support must be validated.

news.title: Seer steers small research agents using predicted tool results and action values
news.summary: A November 19 arXiv preprint introduces reusable offline-trained tool-response and value models that score multiple proposed research actions but execute only the selected tool call. Authors report substantial gains on agent benchmarks for 4B/9B Qwen variants.
news.why_it_matters: Suggests a targeted way to spend local compute on action selection rather than hiring a larger reasoning model or paying for every candidate tool call.
news.caveat: Simulator errors can misrank actions; gains are author-reported in studied benchmarks and no production reliability guarantee or universally usable weights were confirmed.

news.title: GLiDE distills reasoning into single-pass calibrated candidate scoring
news.summary: GLiDE proposes 0.4B–27B decision models that score candidate answers without autoregressive reasoning traces, using partial bidirectional attention and soft-target teacher distillation; the paper reports 92.9 ms median single-GPU latency for its 27B configuration.
news.why_it_matters: Potentially useful for low-latency reranking, grading and discrete choices where full answer generation is unnecessary.
news.caveat: Reported scores and timing are from authors' setup, not a head-to-head universal comparison; model-weight/license availability and calibration transfer remain to be checked.

news.title: R2-VLA conditions robot action on calibrated uncertainty and expert intervention
news.summary: The R2-VLA preprint adds a learned uncertainty predictor and task-level failure-risk calibration to retrieval-based robot policy adaptation; authors report 9.2–11.2 percentage-point success improvements on LIBERO suites.
news.why_it_matters: A concrete design for when a robotic agent should request expert help rather than blindly trusting retrieved demonstrations.
news.caveat: Controlled benchmark results and a stated statistical risk threshold do not certify real-world robot safety under distribution shift.

news.title: Expert-drift study adapts human-AI handoffs as expert reliability changes
news.summary: EDA-L2D models recent expert outcomes when deciding whether a model or human should handle a case; authors evaluate simulated shifts in expert reliability on images, medical tasks and hate-speech data.
news.why_it_matters: A useful challenge to the assumption that human oversight is uniformly reliable at all hours and conditions.
news.caveat: A predictive deferral policy is not proof of safe clinical or legal deployment; the study is a preprint with domain-specific evaluation.

news.title: ScaleWorld shares video prediction and high-resolution refinement in one backbone
news.summary: ScaleWorld proposes a causal video architecture that alternates low-resolution future prediction with one-step high-resolution refinement, trained with task-asymmetric on-policy distillation from specialists.
news.why_it_matters: Combining forecasting and refinement may reduce duplicate models and memory costs for interactive video-world applications.
news.caveat: The efficiency/quality tradeoff is author-reported; no broad hardware throughput replication or production license was independently established.

news.title: Waymo announces two robotaxi safety recalls over lane closures and manual traffic signals
news.summary: Reuters reports Waymo filing two recalls involving closed freeway lanes and responses to officials' manual traffic directions. The company says its freeway-closure remedy is still in work, while the manual-control software update was completed November 6.
news.why_it_matters: An operational example of edge cases where automated driving must handle human-directed traffic control and changing road restrictions.
news.caveat: One crash is tied to the manual-control issue; Waymo reported no collisions/injuries for closed-lane incidents. Distinguish actual recalls from ongoing investigations and Waymo's own safety-performance comparisons.

news.title: South Korean leader spotlights SK–AWS Ulsan data center during construction
news.summary: On November 21 South Korea's president toured a future AI facility in Ulsan, with SK Group and AWS building a data center whose operations were scheduled to begin in late 2027; the project was budgeted at about 7 trillion won through 2029.
news.why_it_matters: Illustrates regional diversification and long lead times for new AI compute capacity beyond chip procurement alone.
news.caveat: Planned capacity, budget and 2027 timing are projections and not already functioning deployed compute.

news.title: Oracle says financing for its OpenAI infrastructure deal is in place
news.summary: In a November 20 statement reported by Reuters, Oracle said funding arrangements for its OpenAI-related data-center contract were in place following its capital raise, while describing future capacity and rack deliveries.
news.why_it_matters: Clarifies a major cloud-compute funding claim while distinguishing contractual finance from operational capacity.
news.caveat: Oracle's financing statement is not independent verification of completion of planned 4.5GW facilities or delivery of Vera Rubin equipment.

technologies.name: Seer (shared decision models)
technologies.explanation: Inference-time research-agent guidance using a reusable tool-response simulator and a value estimator trained offline on trajectories. A host agent proposes actions; Seer estimates outcomes and runs only the selected real call.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Can improve small agents' action choice without executing every candidate web/tool call, when simulations approximate real tool outcomes.
tradeoffs: Simulator/value bias can select harmful actions
alternatives: Tree search with real tool execution
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Requires an underlying research agent plus additional model inference and memory; compute footprint and compatible checkpoints not confirmed.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Source is a preprint; availability/license of any reusable checkpoints or code not verified.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Proposed research method; ready-to-use public implementation not established.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No commercial API price or compute budget verified; local compute costs vary.

technologies.name: GLiDE decision-model family
technologies.explanation: Distilled candidate scorer (0.4B–27B sizes studied) using selective bidirectional attention and soft teacher outputs to make decisions in one forward pass.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Useful when candidate choices are explicit and latency/calibration matters more than free-form generation.
best_fit_uses: Automated classification and grading under a controlled choice set
tradeoffs: Calibration can degrade on unseen distributions
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Studied 0.4B–27B parameters; inference memory and GPU timings depend heavily on precision, batch and device; reported 27B latency is single-GPU experimental.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Preprint does not establish public model license; inspect checkpoints if released.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Availability of weights, inference scripts and hosted endpoints unverified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Pricing not established; local inference may be cheaper for repeated classification but costs are workload-specific.

technologies.name: R2-VLA
technologies.explanation: Robotics adaptation method augmenting a vision-language-action model with retrieved demonstrations, uncertainty estimation, task-level risk calibration and expert corrections.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Supports conditional human intervention rather than blindly running a retrieved-demonstration policy.
tradeoffs: Risk guarantee depends on calibration assumptions
Not demonstrated as a safety-certified real-world robot system
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Requires robot/VLA backbone and retrieval memory, an uncertainty predictor and expert control path; tested on LIBERO simulation suites.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Research proposal only; live robot integration not confirmed.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No official pricing; human-in-the-loop expenses may dominate.

technologies.name: llama.cpp Hibiki duplex integration
technologies.explanation: New mtmd backend support in llama.cpp b12619 for realtime Kyutai Hibiki full-duplex audio, with long-session-quality fixes.
technologies.conditional_advantage: May allow lower-level self-hosted simultaneous-listening-and-speaking workflows without separate complete-turn batching.
tradeoffs: Model checkpoint compatibility must be tested
Hardware audio/compute performance may constrain latency
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Prebuilt llama.cpp binaries cover many CPU/GPU targets but Hibiki duplex model support, RAM/VRAM and audio backend need device-specific verification.
technologies.license_uncertainty: llama.cpp repository license and selected Hibiki model license must be checked separately.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Integration documented in tagged prerelease; production-quality availability unverified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Open-source runtime but hardware and cloud serving costs vary.

terms.name: Expert drift
terms.definition: Changes over time in a human expert's accuracy or decision consistency, which alter whether an AI should defer a task to that expert.
terms.mechanism: A deferral policy uses recent error/outcome history to estimate when human judgments may be more or less reliable.
terms.example: A reviewer becomes less accurate late in a shift; a model reduces automatic handoffs until the human's measured reliability recovers.
terms.caveat: Predicting fatigue or drift from observed outcomes is statistical; it must not be used to stereotype individuals or silently eliminate oversight.

terms.name: Tool-response simulation
terms.definition: Predicting what an external API, web search or other agent tool might return without actually invoking it.
terms.mechanism: A learned model trained on past tool-call/response pairs generates candidate outcome estimates for planning; only chosen actions need real execution.
terms.example: A 4B research agent imagines three possible web searches and executes only the one its separate value model predicts will help most.
terms.caveat: Predicted tool responses are not evidence and must never be cited as if retrieved; inaccurate predictions can worsen search decisions.

terms.name: Risk-calibrated deferral
terms.definition: Setting a model-to-expert handoff threshold from calibration data to target a specified failure-risk bound under stated assumptions.
terms.mechanism: A predictor scores model uncertainty, a calibration procedure chooses the action/ask-human threshold, and new expert corrections can be stored for later retrieval.
terms.example: A robot requests expert correction on risky grasp actions rather than proceeding solely from a retrieved example.
terms.caveat: A calibrated bound under laboratory/task distribution assumptions is not a blanket real-world safety guarantee, especially under distribution shift.
